prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

- Scotland first, independence now: The SNP stands for Scotland, not the London parties that have failed our country. Electing SNP MPs is a vote for independence and for completing the powers of the Scottish Parliament. The more SNP MPs, the stronger the case for a referendum; a majority would trigger one. SNP MPs will always put Scotland first, win more powers, and block anti-Scottish measures.

- A normal nation with modern powers: Independence lets Scotland use its wealth to build a just, caring, enterprising society. The SNP backs a written constitution, inclusive citizenship, proportional representation, and retaining the Queen as Head of State by consent. Scotland’s surplus revenues—especially oil—will be invested for Scotland: a Scottish Fund for Future Generations (oil wealth saved to fund services sustainably) and a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (not‑for‑profit infrastructure finance to outcompete costly PFI/PPP).

- Education and opportunity: Abolish tuition fees and rebuild maintenance grants; create an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18; end misleading league tables; refurbish schools via STPI; statutory duty for Gaelic-medium education.

- Jobs and a Scottish economy: Invest in transport, broadband and skills; streamline development agencies; put tourism marketing under a Scotland-first strategy; devolve/refocus the New Deal; raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages and support small firms; a statutory Charter of Trade Union Rights.

- Environment and energy: Make Scotland a leader in sustainability; audit and deliver a National Environment Plan; 12% of energy and 25% of electricity from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear, decommission existing safely; apply “six Rs”; oppose measures that penalise hydro; regulate MoD pollution.

- Water: End backdoor privatisation and excessive charges; democratise water governance; protect low‑income households.

- NHS you can trust: Establish a National Health Care Commission to end postcode care; free fruit in schools and healthier meals; binding, faster access to approved drugs; restore free dental check‑ups; fair prescription charges; invest via STPI, clean hospitals fund, 1,500 more nurses, halve inpatient waits; free personal care for elderly people.

- Scotland in Europe: Independent Scotland in the EU, supporting a confederal model, subsidiarity, and national vetoes on resources, tax and the constitution; euro only by conditions and referendum; more influence with Scotland’s own votes, Commissioner and full MEP quota.

- Defence and international role: Remove Trident from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; phased withdrawal from NATO’s nuclear structures while cooperating on peacekeeping via EU/UN/OSCE; form a professional Scottish Defence Force; business‑focused external offices; meet UN aid targets, cancel debt, untie aid.

- Culture, language, media, sport: Devolve broadcasting; a “Scottish Six”; digital access for all; national theatre and stronger traditional arts; secure status for Gaelic and promote Scots; Football Academies and a Euro 2008 bid.

- Social justice and housing: A national anti‑poverty strategy and poverty‑proofing; fair, fast asylum system; relieve historic council housing debt, invest via STPI, oppose wholesale stock transfer; support the voluntary sector; tackle homelessness; strengthen equality and disability rights.

- Safer communities: 1,000 extra police; targeted youth justice with parental responsibility orders; lifelong restriction for high‑risk sex offenders; faster courts; keep Scottish fines in Scotland.

- Fair taxation, honest government: No overall tax rise without a mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity; immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut funded by a 5p income tax band over £100k—revenue‑neutral and redistributive.

- Local, rural, primary industries and transport: PR/STV for councils; review local finance incl. local income tax. Cut rural fuel costs; protect post offices, schools and transport; fair EU implementation for farmers; diversify and back organic; reform fisheries with zonal councils and compensated tie‑ups; salmon farming inquiry; stronger community land rights. Modernise rail (reopen lines, electrify) and roads, concessionary fares, reduce ferry fares toward Road Equivalent Tariff, abolish Skye Bridge tolls, boost direct flights.
